name: Ray Charles
milestone_by_age_26: First national hit 'Confession Blues' reached #2 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1949 at age 18; by age 26 he had multiple R&B chart hits including 'Baby Let Me Hold Your Hand' (#5, 1951) and 'I've Got a Woman' (#2, 1954), and was signed to Atlantic Records (1952).
early_history_summary: Charles was born into poverty in rural Georgia and lost his sight by age 7, likely from glaucoma. He attended the Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind from 1937 to 1945, learning piano, saxophone, clarinet, trumpet, and organ. After his mother died in 1945, he began performing professionally, moving to Seattle in 1948 where he formed the McSon Trio and recorded his first hit 'Confession Blues' in 1949 at age 18.
family_context_summary: Born to a laborer and a laundress in rural Georgia; grew up in deep poverty. His younger brother drowned at age 4. His mother died when he was 14, leaving him orphaned and forcing him to support himself through music.

evidence_summary: Ray Charles was born into extreme poverty in rural Georgia and lost his sight by age 7. He received formal musical training at the Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind (1937-1945), learning multiple instruments and Braille music. After his mother's death in 1945, he began performing professionally, moving to Seattle in 1948 where he formed the McSon Trio. His first single 'Confession Blues' reached #2 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1949 at age 18, followed by multiple chart hits through his early twenties. He signed with Atlantic Records in 1952 at age 22. His early success was driven by intense musical specialization from childhood, catalyzed by the adversity of blindness and poverty that channeled him into music.

name: Mercedes Sosa
milestone_by_age_26: Won a singing competition organized by radio station LV12 in Tucumán in 1950 at age 15 under the pseudonym Gladys Osorio, receiving a two-month performance contract that launched a professional singing career spanning over a decade before her first album recording.
early_history_summary: Sosa was born into poverty in San Miguel de Tucumán, Argentina, the daughter of a day laborer and a washerwoman of mestizo (French, Spanish, and Diaguita) descent. At age 15 in 1950, she won a singing competition at radio station LV12, performing under a pseudonym to hide from her father. This launched her professional career, performing on radio and at political events throughout the 1950s. She married guitarist Manuel Oscar Matus in 1957 and became involved in the nuevo cancionero folk movement.
primary_leverage_engine: Vocal talent and early performance experience
family_context_summary: Born to a day laborer (sugarcane cutter) and a washerwoman in Tucumán province, Argentina. Grew up in poverty with mestizo (French, Spanish, and Diaguita indigenous) ancestry. Her parents were Peronists who never registered in the party.

evidence_summary: Mercedes Sosa was born into poverty in Tucumán, Argentina, the daughter of a sugarcane cutter and a washerwoman of mixed indigenous descent. At age 15 in 1950, she won a singing competition at radio station LV12, performing under a pseudonym to hide from her disapproving father. This earned her a two-month contract and launched a professional singing career. She performed on radio and at political events throughout the 1950s, and married guitarist Manuel Oscar Matus in 1957, becoming part of the nuevo cancionero folk movement. Her first album was recorded around 1959-1961 and released in 1962. Her early career was driven by vocal talent and the adversity of poverty and indigenous heritage, with no documented family resources or institutional support.

name: Ron Dennis
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Rondel Racing in 1971 at age 24, a Formula Two team that won five European Championship races and attracted two-time F1 World Champion Graham Hill as a driver, establishing Dennis as a professional team principal in competitive motorsport.

After Jack Brabham retired in 1971, Dennis and colleague Neil Trundle founded Rondel Racing, which became a successful Formula Two team attracting top drivers including Graham Hill and Tim Schenken.

evidence_summary: Ron Dennis entered Formula One at age 18 as a mechanic for Cooper, working alongside driver Jochen Rindt. When Rindt moved to Brabham in 1968, he brought Dennis with him, providing direct exposure to top-tier motorsport operations. After Jack Brabham's retirement in 1971, Dennis and colleague Neil Trundle founded Rondel Racing at age 24, a Formula Two team that won five European Championship races and attracted two-time World Champion Graham Hill. Dennis's early path was defined by deep immersion in the British motorsport ecosystem — the global frontier of Formula One — and a durable partnership with Trundle. No family wealth or motorsport connections are documented; his advantage came from direct domain exposure and the elite performance pipeline of British F1.
